description: Hand-authored expected outcomes for the minimal fixture set. Expectations are derived independently from the definition of Craig interpolation and truth tables; they are NOT produced by the proving core.

cases.rationale: A = a & (!a | d) entails d; B = !d, and d is the only shared variable.
A = p and B = !p conflict directly on the only shared variable.
A = p & !p is contradictory and alphabets are disjoint, so the empty-language interpolant false is forced.
A = p and B = q have disjoint alphabets and are jointly satisfiable (p=q=true); no interpolant exists.
(p & q) is consistent with (p | q), witnessed by p=q=true.
With zero resolutions allowed the engine cannot decide, so it must not emit a proven interpolant.
The pigeonhole-style contradiction needs more than one resolution; a cap of one leaves the result undecided.
Modus ponens: (a -> b) & a entails b, which excludes B = !b.
B = false alone is contradictory; the Pudlak leaf annotation yields the empty-language interpolant true, which excludes B.
